plain: A sailor or soldier who rebels against his officers

webster.text: One guilty of mutiny; a person in military or naval service, who rises in opposition to the authority of the officers, who openly resists the government of the army or navy, or attempts to destroy due subordination.

example.quote: The governour passing by at that time with his guard, seized some of the mutineers and imprisoned them.
example.cite: Letters of Agrippa I-XI, Massachusetts Gazette, Nov. 1787-Jan. 1788
